Express's `app.use(path, subApp)` handles this in `lib/application.js`. When the argument is an app, it sets `mountpath` and `parent` on it. It registers a `mounted_app` wrapper on the router under that path, and that wrapper restores `req` and `res` to the parent app's prototypes afterwards. Then it emits `'mount'` on the sub-app. The `'mount'` handler, set up in the app's init code in the same file, makes the child inherit from the parent. It does this with `Object.setPrototypeOf` on `request`, `response`, `engines` and `settings`, and it also inherits the `trust proxy` setting.

`app.use(path, subapp)` in `lib/application.js` mounts a child app under a URL prefix. It sets `mountpath` and `parent` on the child. It registers a `mounted_app` wrapper on the router at that path, and that wrapper restores `req` and `res` to the parent app's prototypes after the child runs. It then emits `'mount'` on the child. The child's `'mount'` handler, set up in the app init code, sets the prototypes of the child's `request`, `response`, `engines` and `settings` to the parent's. It also drops the child's default `trust proxy` setting so the parent's applies. That is how the child inherits the parent's settings.
